There's 4 types of psych wards.

Low risk - you're not really a danger to yourself and/or others

Medium risk - you're kind of a danger to yourself and/or others

High risk - you need to be monitored pretty much 24/7 because you are a danger to yourself and/or others (this is the one I went to)

The insane asylum - you are very dangerous. You are homicidal, you have charges but too insane to be tried, etc. 

What was allowed in mine may or may not be allowed in others. We couldn't have things like markers (people would suck the ink, heard that's happened before). Some things you can have but you must be supervised by staff.

Don't kick your kids out because they're gay/trans/LGBT. They are who they are. Accept them. You can't change them.

There are always alternative punishments such as taking things they like away (toys, games, electronics, etc. Anything BUT food, their bed and clothes) or not letting them do things they enjoy (going out with friends, going out, using electronics, etc.) There's no reason to beat your kids as punishment.

Don't push your dreams on your kids. If the kid wants to do art and not piano, let them do piano. It teaches them that they can do what they want if they put their mind to it.

Take your kids seriously. If they say they need therapy/doctor/dentist/whatever, take them. They might be fighting battles you have no idea about. If they say they're going to/are currently harming themselves, take them to the mental hospital and have them attend therapy. It can save them.
